name: APS – Saver Choice Max / Time-of-Use 4pm–7pm with Demand (summer)
assumed: Two things, one of them a grammar limit worth reading. (1) The price: $19.585/kW is APS's summer R-3 demand rate as reported secondarily (Decision 79293, effective 2024-03-08); the APS rate-schedule PDF was not read, so the household's own plan sheet replaces it. The window — the highest hour between 4pm and 7pm on weekdays, a 60-minute demand interval, the single highest of the billing month — is APS's own, from aps.com/demand, and is not assumed. (2) The season: this version covers **summer only** (May–October). APS also charges a demand rate in winter, at a lower $/kW, and `PeakTariff` carries one `pricing` and one `eligible` per version, so one file cannot hold both — a version is dated, and a season recurs. Rather than apply the summer price year-round (which would defend the right hours at the wrong price) or invent a winter figure, the eligible months stop at October: a winter month has no capacity component and the site steers on price alone, which is the documented degradation (HLD §3) and not a wrong number. What would remove this note is a seasonal `pricing` in the grammar, which is D2's call and not this WP's. Arizona does not observe DST, so America/Phoenix needs no seam care.

versions.assumed: See the file-level note: summer season only, and the $/kW is secondary.
